headline: Independent (non-runtime) re-derivation of the CRO signed-packet binding contract reproduces candidate_sha256, formula_sha256, the byte-exact canonical rendering, and the Ed25519 signature of the known-answer fixture, and confirms 12/12 tamper probes fail closed -- corroborating that candidate+formula binding yields an unambiguous, fully-numeric, tamper-evident CRO lab packet.
non_circularity: Oracle is a fresh Python implementation over CPython stdlib json/hashlib and off-the-shelf cryptography 41.0.7 Ed25519; it consumes only the on-disk fixture bytes and never the shipped Rust runtime. The rendering re-derivation was authored from published formatting, not copied from runtime output.
purpose: Provide a second independent decider of the packet-binding hypothesis using only published primitives (FIPS 180-4, RFC 8032, RFC 8785), without invoking the Rust runtime, so the module's central claim is cross-checked rather than self-attested.
theory_reference: IETF RFC 8032 (2017) Edwards-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (Ed25519); Bernstein et al. CHES 2011
